title: Trabeculectomy: The Gold Standard Filtration Surgery
summary: Trabeculectomy remains the definitive glaucoma filtration procedure, establishing a controlled fistula between the anterior chamber and subconjunctival space. Mastering the balance between aqueous outflow and scarring is the cornerstone of successful long-term IOP control.

sections.title: Indications for Surgery
content: Progression of glaucomatous optic neuropathy despite maximum tolerated medical therapy.
Inability to tolerate topical anti-glaucoma medications (e.g., ocular surface disease).
Target IOP not achieved despite selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT).
Poor patient compliance with chronic drop regimen.
Need for low target IOP (e.g., advanced disease with narrow rim).

sections.title: Absolute & Relative Contraindications
content: Active external ocular infection (Blepharitis, Conjunctivitis).
Neovascular glaucoma (relative, often requires MIGS/tube first).
Severe conjunctival scarring (precludes successful bleb formation).
Patient unable to remain supine/cooperate during surgery.
Risk of profound hypotony (e.g., high myopia, underlying scleral pathology).

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Step-by-Step
content: Step 1: Conjunctival peritomy (limbal-based or fornix-based).
Step 2: Mitomycin-C application (usually 0.2–0.4 mg/ml for 1–3 mins).
Step 3: Scleral flap creation (approx. 3x3 mm partial thickness).
Step 4: Paracentesis entry.
Step 5: Sclerostomy (punching the block) & peripheral iridectomy (PI).
Step 6: Scleral flap closure with releasable 10-0 nylon sutures.
Step 7: Water-tight conjunctival closure (running or interrupted sutures).

content.explanation: S: Steroids (frequent topical), T: Topical Antibiotics, A: Avoid pressure/rubbing, M: Monitor IOP/Seidel, P: Pupil dilation (if synechiae).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Success
content: A well-functioning bleb is diffuse, vascular, and non-cystic.
Always assess the bleb morphology using the 'Indiana Bleb Appearance Grading Scale'.
Early post-op: Use laser suture lysis if IOP remains elevated at 1-2 weeks.
If Seidel is positive, consider pressure patching or bandage contact lens.
Prophylactic antibiotic use should continue until the conjunctival wound is fully epithelized.
